assertion: The federal budget deficit totaled $404 billion during the first month (October) of fiscal year 2027 – $120 billion higher than the corresponding period in FY 2026.
independent_value: Treasury MTS Table 1: Oct FY27 deficit 404,063,547,878; Oct FY26 284,332,743,998

assertion: The FY 2027 deficit was the net effect of $773 billion of spending and $369 billion of revenue collections.
Federal revenue collections fell by $35 billion (9 percent) during the first month of FY 2027 compared to last year.
Federal spending rose by $84 billion (12 percent) during the first month of FY 2027 compared to the corresponding period last year.
Individual income tax receipts decreased by $31 billion (14 percent) while payroll tax collections rose by $4 billion (3 percent).
inaccuracy: The claim says payroll tax rose $4B (3%); Treasury shows employment and general retirement +$4.8B (+3.9%) and all social insurance +$3.2B (+2.5%). Individual income tax (-$30.6B, -14.1%) is exact.

assertion: Corporate income tax receipts increased by $3 billion (20 percent). Estate and gift taxes remained flat at $4 billion, excise tax collections held steady at $6 billion, and other sources of revenue increased by $1 billion (18 percent).
Customs duties fell by $12 billion (39 percent) due to tariff changes made through executive action.
inaccuracy: The claim says tariff changes through executive action drove the drop; the figure is right (-12.1B, -38.7%) but net customs also reflect court-ordered refunds, and the split is not quantified.
independent_value: Customs down; refunds since May per Tax Foundation

sources.title: Tax Foundation on refunds since May

assertion: Notably, customs duties have declined since May as the federal government issued tariff refunds to businesses that paid tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, which the Supreme Court ruled illegal.
inaccuracy: The claim says customs declined since May; Treasury shows net customs falling from February-March, bottoming at -25.6B in June, and recovering to 19.2B by October.
warehouse_value: Monthly net customs: Apr 22.1, May -0.04, Jun -25.6, Jul -8.5, Aug 12.8, Sep 5.9, Oct 19.2 ($B)
independent_value: Refunds began May 2026; SCOTUS 6-3 on Feb 20, 2026

assertion: Social Security spending increased by $9 billion (6 percent) due to increases in average monthly benefits and the number of beneficiaries enrolled in the program. Medicare spending rose by $19 billion (13 percent) due to higher enrollment and payment rates for services, and Medicaid spending increased by $7 billion (13 percent) because of higher per-enrollee costs. Other health spending, including on the Children’s Health Insurance Program and Affordable Care Act premium tax credits, declined by $2 billion (5 percent).
warehouse_value: SS +8.5B (+6.4%); Medicare +19.5B (+12.9%); Medicaid base 55.8B so +7B = 12.5%; Health function +5.4B net
independent_value: MTS Table 5 Oct 2025 Medicaid 55.78B; magnitudes consistent. Causes are the author's attribution, not contradicted.

assertion: National defense spending increased by $29 billion (29 percent) due to higher spending on military personnel and research and development. Spending on veterans’ benefits and services rose by $5 billion (9 percent) because more people received benefits and spending per beneficiary rose. Spending on income security programs, including the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, Supplemental Security Income, and Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, fell by $4 billion (6 percent) in part because of the One Big Beautiful Bill’s reforms to certain income security programs. Other programmatic spending rose by $9 billion (67 percent).
independent_value: MTS Table 9; causes are author attribution, not contradicted

assertion: Interest payments on the national debt increased by $12 billion (13 percent) because the debt was larger and long-term interest rates were higher.
During the first month of FY 2027, net interest was the fourth-largest government expenditure behind Medicare, Social Security, and national defense.
warehouse_value: Medicare 170.0, SS 142.7, Defense 128.9, Net interest 103.1, Health 93.5
